groups.name: Agents · Bedrock AgentCore
groups.note: Two agents, one per API. Both stacks are the same shape; they differ only in name, model and bundled package.

d.role: Hosts one Strands agent, invoked by the API and streaming AG-UI events back.
facts: The runtime name may not contain dashes, so the construct replaces them with underscores.

d.role: Holds the turns of a conversation so the next question has context.
facts: Events expire after 90 days. Nothing in the repository deletes memory when a conversation is deleted through an API.

groups.name: APIs · API Gateway, Cognito and Lambda

d.role: Two routes: invoke, which streams the answer back, and messages, which reads a conversation. Behind a Web ACL and stage throttling.
threads/invoke, which streams, and threads/messages, which reads a conversation back.
facts: Neither sets a memory size, so both take the CDK default.
The invoke timeout and the run lock lease are the same thirty seconds.

d.role: One pool, two clients: the API's, client credentials only, with a resource server chat-api and one scope, invoke; and the UI's sign-in client, code flow with PKCE and the scope openid.
facts: Access tokens last an hour in staging and production, and a day in ephemeral environments.

d.role: Threads, runs, locks and messages in one table with a one-year TTL.
facts: Retained outside ephemeral environments; destroyed with the stack in them.

groups.name: UI · ECS Express, VPC and Secrets Manager

d.tech: a Docker image built from the repository root
d.role: The Next.js web app, health-checked on /api/health, with the session secret injected and a month of logs.
facts: Scales between one task and one task.
Three roles: execution, task, and an infrastructure role for ECS itself.

d.tech: created for the ECS service alone
d.role: The only network this repository creates. Nothing private, so nothing needs a NAT gateway.
The key the UI seals its session cookie with. The API app client's secret is not here: it lives in Cognito and is read from there.

items.name: Sign-in clients
meta: callback set by a custom resource

d.role: How a person signs in to the web app. Its callback and logout URLs are written after deploy, once the service's endpoint exists.
facts: An ephemeral environment also allows http://localhost:3000, so the app can run locally against a deployed stack.

d.role: More than fifteen POST /v1/threads/invoke in a minute from one end-user-id answers 429 with a JSON body.
facts: The limits are V1's (CHAT-968), carried over: 900 a minute per client, 15 a minute per end user.
